stories.title: In Venezuela, silence has become a rescue tool
stories.summary: In Venezuela rescue crews now stop almost everything and ask for silence so they can hear anyone still alive underneath the rubble. NPR's Eyder Peralta reports from the port city of La Guaira.

stories.title: The World Cup spotlights Indigenous cultures
stories.summary: As the World Cup comes to the Pacific Northwest, Indigenous people are welcoming fans with ceremonies, music and culture while sharing the history of the land. Lauren Gallup reports from Seattle.

stories.title: A bridge to Canada may be blocked by the Trump administration
stories.summary: The Gordie Howe bridge spans the most important border crossing between the U.S. and Canada. President Donald Trump has said he doesn't want it open yet.

stories.title: Beyond the Shore podcast uncovers the hidden world of the Great Lakes
stories.summary: In Michigan Public's new podcast Beyond the Shore, host Rebecca Williams uncovers the shipwrecks, remarkable wildlife and hidden ecosystems beneath America's Great Lakes.

stories.title: What the TPS ruling means for Haitian immigrants
stories.summary: The Supreme Court cleared the way for the Trump administration to end TPS protections for hundreds of thousands of people. Rep. Ayanna Presley talks about what it will mean for Haitian families.

stories.title: As America turns 250, protesters make their case
stories.summary: Demonstrators gathered in cities across the U.S. today say they're offering a different vision for America ahead of its 250th birthday than the Trump administration's Freedom 250 events. NPR's Marissa Lang visited one rally near the White House.
